chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Layth al-Muradi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave woman, is her divorce valid? He said: If she is your slave, then no, for Allah the Exalted says: 'A slave who has no power over anything.' And if she is the slave of other people, or a free woman, then her divorce is valid.
ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of a slave woman valid if she is owned by her husband?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a slave woman owned personally by her husband lacks independent legal capacity ('la yaqdiru ala shay'), rendering her divorce invalid as it is contingent on the owner's will. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that personal ownership of a slave creates a unique marital bond where the husband's authority supersedes the slave's agency, unlike slaves owned by others or free women who possess greater legal autonomy.
